Parameter values are chosen to keep the dynamics physical and visibly nontrivial without driving the system into pathological saturation. With T_A(0)=400 K and T_B(0)=350 K, the mean temperature is 375 K, so 1 + conductance_temp_coeff*(T_A+T_B)/2 ≈ 1.375, giving a noticeable but moderate mean-temperature modulation. The time range 0–300 with 301 points should capture the early conductance-relaxation transient, the mid-course change in normalized rate as contrast decays, and the late approach toward common temperature. This plan exposes the intended generation-5 distinction through reachable states within one trajectory family: as the isolated pair evolves, both contrast and mean temperature change, so the scored target samples a mean-temperature-modulated contrast-saturation law rather than a single global contrast curve.
